transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Redwood Solutions), Mark Reynolds (OptiRetail CTO), Sofia Lopez (OptiRetail Head of Infra), Daniel Wu (OptiRetail ML Eng), Priya Kumar (OptiRetail Security)

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna do a deep dive on Dedicated versus Hosted focusing on runtime performance -- latency, throughput, kv cache, batching and quantization and the vpc/on-prem implications. mark, do you want to kick off with your primary concerns?
00:18 Mark (OptiRetail - CTO): yeah thanks, alex. main concerns are predictable p95/p99 tail latency for our search ranking model and noisy neighbor issues. we run spikes around midnight and during promotions, so throughput guarantees matter. cost also matters but reliability first.
00:36 Sofia (Head of Infrastructure): and for us security: vpc peering, kms for keys, and audit logs. we also would consider an on-prem option for a subset of traffic.
00:50 Priya (Redwood SE): great, that's our usual set. quick context: our Hosted offering gives fast time-to-value with shared pools and autoscaling; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with isolation and SLA-backed throughput targets. we'll go through latency profiles, KV cache behavior, batching, and quantization impacts.
01:12 Alex: note that some transcription may flip product names, you'll hear 'Redwood Dedicate' occasionally, sorry in advance.
01:20 Priya (SE): starting with overall latency breakdown: we measure p50, p95, p99 token latency across components: network (client->gateway), routing & queuing, model runtime (attention compute), and post-processing. In Hosted, the routing layer may route to multiple tenants, so queueing-induced tail latency can appear during noisy neighbors. Dedicated reduces that by isolating GPUs and giving predictable queueing.
02:05 Daniel (ML Eng): can you quantify what predictable means? like, do you give per-GPU qps guarantees or per-tenant throughput?
02:18 Priya: we provide throughput guardrails per Dedicated pool. Typically we size pools to hit a committed QPS or tokens/sec; on top of that we offer burst capacity. For example, for a 8xA100 pool pinned to a single tenant we can guarantee sustained tokens/sec with a documented p95 latency envelope for a given model and prompt length. exact numbers depend on model, sequence length, and quantization.
02:47 Mark: how hard is it to reproduce our model behavior? our ranking model has variable sequence lengths 64-1024 and some sessions reuse long contexts.
03:00 Priya: good question. sequence length distribution matters a lot. the runtime has kernel selection and compilation strategies that choose execution paths based on sequence length; longer contexts increase memory and KV cache usage. in Dedicated we can pin model versions and kernel profiles which reduces runtime variance.
03:26 Maya (Redwood): also worth noting kv cache: Hosted caches are per-request prefix and we do cross-request KV caching when possible, but eviction policies are shared across tenants. Dedicated allows you to enable private persistent KV cache with higher hit-rate guarantees because fewer competing prefixes evict each other.
03:52 Sofia: so does Dedicated actually let us pin a customer-wide kv cache so repeated sessions get near 100% hits? we care about session reuse for personalization.
04:05 Priya: you can get much higher hit rates. we offer warmup strategies and pre-populating caches for hot prefixes; with Dedicated we can also configure cache sizes and TTLs per tenant. it's not always 100% but for many workloads we see big reductions in per-token compute.
04:25 Daniel: what about batching? our burst pattern means short bursts of small requests, which are bad for throughput unless you batch. we can't add latency at tail.
04:38 Priya: runtime does continuous batching. We offer suggestions for batching window (e.g., 10-30ms) which trades a small latency increase for big throughput gains. Dedicated gives more consistent batching efficiency because the runtime is serving only your traffic and batch formation is predictable. In Hosted, batch formation is dynamic and influenced by other tenants' traffic.
05:05 Alex: quick interruption: common industrial tradeoff is latency vs cost. for lower cost we recommend slightly larger batching with aggressive KV caching and quantization; for lowest latency you pick Dedicated with minimal batching and possibly model distillation.
05:26 Mark: quantization -- we want to understand quality regression risks. can you run 4-bit quant with our model?
05:34 Priya: we support per-layer quantization strategies. many customers successfully run 4-bit quant (QLoRA-like) with minimal accuracy loss for ranking and reranking, but we recommend running a quality regression suite. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles; in Dedicated you can pin a quantized variant and validate on your evals before rollout.
05:58 Daniel: do kernel optimizations differ between quantized and fp16?
06:05 Priya: yes, execution paths are different. quantized kernels avoid some FP ops and reduce memory bandwidth; that usually improves throughput and lowers latency per token. but some attention fusions behave differently so measuring on your prompts is critical.
06:28 Sofia: noisy neighbor specifics: If another tenant saturates GPU memory or causes CPU scheduling pressure, how do you prevent that? we want hard isolation.
06:39 Priya: Dedicated pools are tenant-dedicated VMs/GPU nodes. isolation is achieved at the allocation layer: your workloads don't share the same GPU processes with other tenants. Noisy neighbor in Dedicated is limited to workloads within your own pool (i.e., your apps). For Hosted, we have isolation limits but it's multi-tenant so imperfect. Also Dedicated includes resource reservations and cgroup constraints to prevent CPU/IO interference.
07:12 Mark: and for on-prem / VPC deployment, can we run the same runtime and get similar guarantees?
07:19 Maya: yes, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) runs the same serving runtime. However, SLA and autoscaling behaviors differ because we can't control customer hardware. We provide configuration guidance, kernel selection tooling, and a private control plane option to manage rollouts and tracing. For strict SLAs you may want Dedicated in our cloud or a tightly specified on-prem hardware bill of materials.
07:47 Daniel: what about KV cache persistence across restarts or pod evictions? if a node reboots we lose cache and hit rates drop.
07:58 Priya: in Dedicated we offer optional persistent cache tiering (disk-backed, optional NVRAM) that allows cache recovery; plus we do graceful draining and warm start policies to reduce cold-cache penalties. In Hosted, we have aggressive pooling and warm-up heuristics but you don't control persistence.
08:22 Mark: measuring tail latency: what telemetry should we send you to reproduce?
08:29 Priya: send 1) request traces with timestamps (client send, gateway recv, runtime start/end), 2) QPS profile over time, 3) sequence length histogram, 4) example prompts. we'll run a benchmark with identical model and quantization settings to reproduce p50/p95/p99.
08:47 Alex: we'll provide a bench script; priya will prepare a harness that simulates your bursty traffic and the KV warmup patterns.
08:56 Daniel: how do you handle model pinning and rollouts? we want to do canary and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant if latency spikes.
09:05 Priya: we support rollout policies: canary by percentage, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants (e.g., fp16 fallback if a quantized backend fails). You can also route by policy (latency-first vs cost-first).
09:22 Sofia: routing by region matters for us for data residency. Hosted can route requests to different regions, but Dedicated is region pinned; is there cross-region failover?
09:33 Maya: yes, Dedicated pools are region-scoped, but we support cross-region failover policies and multi-pool deployments. for strict residency you can keep primary region only.
09:44 Mark: any gotchas on network egress or peering for Dedicated?
09:50 Alex: we'll share a network checklist. Dedicated often needs VPC peering, specific port ranges, NAT config for outbound access to control plane, and allowed egress to KMS endpoints. We'll put that in the next-step docs.
10:05 Priya: switching to concrete numbers: for a mid-size ranking model (1.2B, sequence length 256), an 8xA100 Dedicated pool with 4-bit quant can sustain ~X tokens/sec (we used placeholders in recorded call) with p95 under 120ms in our bench; on Hosted p95 tends to be higher variance due to queueing. we will produce model-specific numbers after running your traces.
10:35 Daniel: are there automated recommendations to tune batching and cache sizes?
10:41 Priya: Redwood Optimize does that—it analyzes traces and suggests batching window, cache size, and quant profile. in Dedicated we can apply those automatically or as a suggested runbook.
10:52 Mark: what's the impact of session affinity? we need affinity for personalization to keep cache hits.
10:58 Priya: we support sticky routing for sessions and connection-level affinity; it's stronger in Dedicated because you control the pool. affinity reduces batchability slightly but improves cache hit rate; it's a tradeoff.
11:16 Sofia: security: SOC2, audit logs, SAML SSO, and KMS integration. any friction we should be aware of?
11:25 Alex: Hosted supports SOC2 and SAML; Dedicated and Private provide additional integrations with customer-managed KMS and audit log retention options. for Private on-prem you'll integrate your own HSM or KMS endpoints. we'll send the security pack.
11:38 Priya Kumar (OptiRetail Security): about encryption in transit and at rest, does Dedicated store any persistent PII in logs?
11:46 Alex: logs are configurable; we can mask or avoid storing PII. audit logs can be delivered to your SIEM. we'll include retention and masking options in the security doc.
11:58 Mark: Operationally, how do upgrades happen? we don't want unexpected model/serving changes during peak.
12:06 Maya: Dedicated supports scheduled maintenance windows; we offer controlled rollout with canary and automatic rollback. for mission-critical windows we can coordinate freeze periods.
12:18 Daniel: final question: what's the typical lead time to provision a Dedicated pool?
12:23 Alex: depends on region and capacity, but typically 2-6 weeks for larger reserved pools. we can sometimes do a smaller pilot within a few days for early benchmarking.
12:34 Priya: recap of recommended approach for OptiRetail: 1) start with a Hosted pilot to validate correctness and quick benchmarks, 2) run a Dedicated benchmark with your traces and apply Redwood Optimize recommendations, 3) move critical production traffic to Dedicated pools with KV persistent cache and pinned quantized model variants, 4) enable session affinity for personalization, 5) use canary rollouts and rollback policies.
12:58 Alex: ok we'll follow up: action items and docs as recorded. thanks everyone.
13:04 Mark: thanks all, that was helpful.
13:10 meeting end

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions present (product names, numbers as X in call); some timestamps rounded.
